bias_designer: Strong, and it inflates B's lead. CONCEPTS.md gives B about 355 words, against about 206 for A and about 178 for C. Several capabilities appear only in B's text, even though the header says all three share the same platform. (1) Only B's approver screen has an independent checker: 'Beside each finding: its evidence, the independent checker's verdict, and warnings (old data, unsupported number)'. A gets only '[Approve & send] [Edit] [Reject]' and 'scrolls the thread for context', and C gets 'comments sidebar and an [Approve] button for the whole report'. So P7's catch_stale (B yes, A and C unlikely) comes from the spec, not the layout. No layout catches stale data without a staleness checker. (2) Only B has a 'Needs you' queue that includes 'Client stuck 3 days on data', so notice_stuck=yes is also written into the spec. (3) Only B's data items have 'why we need it / how to get it (step-by-step for Shopify/Odoo/Excel) / Someone else has this → invite them / We don't have it → what happens instead / Must have vs Helpful / example of a correct file / saves automatically'. A gives only a reason line plus '[I don't have this]' with no consequence stated, and C gives 'name, description, status, upload button'. (4) Only B has per-finding confidence ('Strong/Moderate/Weak/Not yet tested… what would make it stronger') and '[Ask a question]' per finding. C puts confidence in an 'appendix', and A shows none. (5) Only B mentions WhatsApp, and only B lists 'Word' and an '[Arabic version]' button for the report. A's report is 'a long chat message… [Download PDF]'. Persona quotes credit exactly these bolt-ons: P1 'push the Odoo stuff to my accountant' (invite), P3 'invite my colleague… confidence per finding protects me', P5 'it said we're not sure about the ads part' (per-finding confidence plus 'don't have it'), P7 'the warning sits next to the number'. If A and C were specified fairly, the gap would mostly close on trust and approver metrics and would narrow on completion. A with a pinned 'next step plus outstanding items' panel would probably fix the 'scroll forever' complaints from P1, P5 and P6. C would stay weakest because of the upfront wizard and the dashboard of percentages, which are structural problems.

structural: One page per engagement that you come back to after days, with no scrolling through a thread (A's 'scroll up forever' complaints from P1, P5 and P6)

A 'Your next step' card that is always on top and says who owns the next action (the most cited win; it also works as a landmark for P6). A chat can copy this as a pinned header, so it is only partly unique to B
Starting with free text plus 3–5 follow-up questions instead of a 5-step wizard (this is what beats C)
A persistent data checklist as a list rather than messages, which lets P6 find pending items
A progress tracker in words rather than percentage tiles (this beats C's dashboard)
Approval per finding rather than per message (A) or per whole report (C)
bolt_on: Invite a colleague or data owner (could be added to A or C)
'Why we need it' and 'how to get it' per data item, plus Must/Helpful labels and an example of a correct file
'We don't have it → what happens instead'
Confidence per finding with a reason and what would make it stronger (C could move it from the appendix to each finding; A could add it inline)
'Ask a question' per finding (A has this natively)
An independent checker plus stale or unsupported-number warnings (a backend capability that suits any UI)
Exceptions queue with stuck-client timers (C's admin table could sort by flags)
Word and Arabic report export (C already has formal PDF/Word)

bias_persona: There are strong signs of model homogeneity and textbook bias. All six client personas give B exactly trust=4 and give C between 3 and 4, with no variance and no outlier who loves chat or hates B. They all write in the same polished, well-structured voice, and their wishlists converge on the same items: a named human sign-off (P1–P5), confidence per finding (P2, P3, P4, P6), and a source for every number (P2, P3, P4, P6, P7). These read like Nielsen heuristics (visibility of system status, 'tell me what to do next', 'colour isn't information') rather than idiosyncratic behaviour. The phone-first SME owner (P1) and founder (P5) both pick a long single page over texting, while P7 notes that 'the page gets long for P1/P5 on a phone'. Real behaviour often goes the other way. Chat is the dominant interface people actually use (ChatGPT, and WhatsApp-native commerce in the UAE, where P1's staff 'live in WhatsApp'). Low-effort conversational intake usually beats structured pages on starting, and starting is where funnels die. Enterprise buyers (P2, P3, P4 types) often do like dashboards and formal portals, and procurement expects them. Many executive buyers never log in at all: they get a PDF or email and a meeting. The personas also judged text descriptions, not prototypes, so the long-page cost, scrolling and empty states were never felt. 'Completion' is the LLM's self-prediction, n=6, from one model. The pre-registered T1/T2 validity checks must be shown to have passed before any of this counts even as Level B.
missing_cases: A client who wants to just talk or think aloud. They would find B's form-like page cold, and A wins for them
An economic buyer who never logs in (CEO or board) and only reads email or PDF or attends a meeting. B's web page is invisible to them; a read-only board seat (P2) or an email digest is needed
Mobile-only users across the whole engagement (P1, P5). Uploads, a long page and the report on a phone were never tested
Several stakeholders with conflicting views of the problem (the CFO versus the plant manager): who edits 'What we understood'? Roles, permissions and edit conflicts are absent
A data owner who is invited but is not a buyer (an IT person, analyst or accountant): their own onboarding, and the 'hasn't uploaded yet' state
A client who reframes the problem midway (H2, the 003 reframe at 2h15m): B's fixed tracker has no clear 'restart framing' path
A client with no data at all, or only qualitative knowledge: the checklist may be mostly 'don't have it'
A repeat client running several engagements: portfolio view and history
Arabic-first users on mobile and the RTL long page. Only P3 tested Arabic, on a desktop
A procurement or legal reviewer who needs the contract, DPA and security pack before any login
The founder approving on a phone between meetings (P7 asked for this)
Low digital literacy, voice-first users (WhatsApp voice notes were requested by P1 and P5)
A client who disputes an approved finding and wants it renegotiated (P7 flagged the 'Ask a question' reopening risk)
H0_verdict: Partly supported, and mostly not about screen layout. When asked what makes them quit, about 4 of 7 personas named non-layout dealbreakers. P2: patient-data governance or a DPO workaround. P3: no security or data-residency pack, or an English-only report. P4 and P7: any number that can't be traced to its source or labelled as an assumption. P1: manual exports, which is about data connectors. Only P5 (a hard required field) and P6 (lost work, drag-only upload) are pure UX. P2 and P3 needed outside help in every concept because of organisational approvals, which no layout fixes. What actually drives trust and completion is the evidence pipeline: number lineage, a stale-data checker, access to data, governance and approvals, a formal Arabic deliverable, and a provisional or quick-win result before all the data arrives. UX matters as the carrier of 'who owns the next action', but the business rests on traceable, approvable analysis and a short time to first value. A better phrasing of H0: 'experience design, including data and governance flows, matters; screen layout is secondary.'
mvp_must: One page per engagement (B structure) with a 'next step' card always on top that shows the owner and time estimate, collapsed completed sections, and mobile layout
Free-text intake plus 3–5 follow-up questions, and a confirmable 'what we understood' section
Data checklist: why, how, Must/Helpful, upload with plain errors and a text example, 'we don't have it → what happens instead', autosave
Invite one extra user by email to supply data (for the CFO's analyst and the SME's accountant), with a 'done or pending' state. A simple link invite is enough
Report: one-paragraph answer, steps, confidence per finding with a reason, and a source or 'ASSUMPTION' tag with an as-of date on every number

Approver review per finding: evidence plus source and date per number, a basic staleness rule (for example older than 30 days triggers a warning), auto-flagging of numbers with no trace, release blocked until each warning is resolved, and an approve-all-clean action
An approver queue with stuck clients (separating expected waits from silence) and reports ready to review
Email notifications only when the client has an action or a result is ready, with a deep link to the next step
PDF and Word export with Arabic/RTL support, at least for the report
WCAG 2.2 AA basics: headings and landmarks, text status rather than colour, unique control names, persistent inline errors, keyboard upload
A static security, data-handling and residency one-pager in English and Arabic, and a named consultant sign-off on the report
Price and turnaround shown up front, and one sample report
mvp_later: A scenario sandbox that recalculates NPV/IRR and an editable assumptions table (P4)
WhatsApp notifications or replies, and voice notes
On-premise or offline mode, and Arabic official data-request letters
A read-only board seat, fine-grained roles, and a signed audit trail (log approvals in the database now; add the UI later)
A diff of what changed since the approver last saw a draft, a time-spent counter, and a portfolio slippage strip
A 5-slide leadership deck and a bilingual glossary
Auto-generated governance pack per client (start with a static one)
A 'start with aggregate or de-identified data' provisional mode (design for it in the data model; full flow later), unless hospitals or government are the first segment
Native OAuth connectors beyond one (start with uploads plus Shopify or Google Sheets at most)
Per-finding chat panel (use 'Ask a question' that goes to the approver queue first)
An accessibility preference profile and an audio briefing
sales_killers_if_missing: Number traceability (a source or ASSUMPTION tag on every number) plus a named human sign-off. Without these the CFO and other skeptics walk away, and the founder's own 'never send a wrong claim' promise fails
A security, data-handling and residency pack. Without it government and hospital buyers cannot even start procurement
An Arabic formal Word/PDF deliverable. Without it the government segment is closed
A sample report and visible price and turnaround before signup. Without them SME and startup buyers won't commit to an unknown
A way forward when data is missing or delayed (a 'don't have it' path or provisional result). Without it the 2–6 week waits kill momentum and renewals
Save and resume, plus clarity on the next action. Without them the 15-minute-burst users abandon
most_likely_wrong: The decision ranks layouts when the outcome is driven by something else. B's 4/6 versus 1/6 lead is mostly an artefact of features specified only for B (checker warnings, invite, why/how, per-finding confidence, Word/Arabic, a stuck-client queue), judged by six instances of one LLM that reward textbook UX. A fairly specified chat-first hybrid, a conversation plus a pinned next-step and checklist panel, would likely tie B and could beat it for the phone-first SME and startup buyers, who are probably the fastest first sales. Meanwhile the real failure mode is upstream of any screen: the founder cannot yet produce traceable, checker-verified numbers within one approver-hour, the first segment (E1) is unknown, and the enterprise segments are gated by governance and Arabic deliverables, not page layout.
required_changes: Run a parity re-test: rewrite A and C with the same bolt-on features (invite, why/how, 'don't have it', per-finding confidence, checker warnings, stuck queue, Word/Arabic, WhatsApp) and re-run personas. Report how much of B's lead remains after that

Test a hybrid of B's page with a conversational intake and an 'Ask' panel, which the pre-registration allows, built from B's next-step and checklist parts and A's intake. Run its second simulated pass

Reword the conclusion: B wins on structure for status and resumption. Most of the measured trust and approver gains come from the evidence pipeline (number lineage, staleness checker, per-finding approval), which is the real MVP core and works with any UI
Downgrade H0 to 'partly supported'. List governance, the security pack, the Arabic formal deliverable and number traceability as co-equal or higher drivers
Report P2 and P3 'with_help' as an organisational ceiling, not a UI failure, and report completion as 4 of the 4 clients who could complete versus 1 of 4 for A
Report the score uniformity (all six give B trust 4) and the same-model caveat. Show T1/T2 validity results before ranking, and keep the claim at Level B

Add missing personas or situations before committing: a buyer who never logs in, a client who wants to just chat, a mobile-only engagement end to end, multiple stakeholders with conflicting framings, and an invited non-buyer data owner

Get the founder's answer to E1 (the first segment) before scoping. If the first sales are SMEs, prioritise mobile, WhatsApp-style messaging and quick wins; if government or hospitals, prioritise the security pack, Arabic Word and governance-aware data states
Validate with 5 real users from the first segment on a clickable prototype before engineering builds anything
